title: A SNV-accessible mutational scan of human PSAT1 using functional complementation in yeast.
methodText: Yeast strains were arrayed and grown on solid minimal medium lacking serine. Strain growth was measured by an automated image analysis pipeline (https://github.com/lacyk3/PyPl8/tree/main/src/PyPl8), and adjusted for plate, neighbor, and edge effects. Growth scores were then normalized to 0-1 scale where 0 corresponds to null controls and 1 corresponds to WT controls.
abstractText: Pathogenic variants in PHGDH, PSAT1, and PSPH cause a set of rare, autosomal recessive diseases known as serine biosynthesis defects. However, because L-serine supplementation, especially if started early, can ameliorate and in some cases even prevent symptoms, knowledge of pathogenic variants is highly actionable. Here, we apply a yeast complementation assay to measure the functional impact of 1,914 SNV-accessible amino acid substitutions in human PSAT, corresponding to ~88% of all unique SNV-accessible amino acid substitutions (n=2,182) in the human PSAT1 cDNA sequence. Results of our assay of individual variants (in haploid yeast cells) agree well with existing clinical interpretations and known protein structure-function relationships.
shortDescription: A SNV-accessible mutational scan of human PSAT1 using functional complementation in yeast via a solid growth assay.
